title: His Father Left the Stadium Out of Superstition. His Son Took Seven Wickets on Debut.
excerpt: Manav Suthar, a schoolteacher's son from Rajasthan's border town of Sri Ganganagar, became Player of the Match in India's largest-ever Test win. His family had gone home before the first ball was bowled.
body:
Manav Suthar's phone rang after stumps on Day 2 of the one-off Test against Afghanistan at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in New Chandigarh. He had just taken three wickets for 21 runs in 15.5 overs on debut. On the other end were his parents — watching from home in Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, a small city on the India-Pakistan border known more for its mustard fields than its cricketers.

They had been in the stadium that morning. Then they left.

"Yes, me, my wife, my daughter Mansi had come to watch his debut. I can't describe how it felt seeing him get the Test cap," his father Jagdish Suthar, a retired physical education teacher, told PTI. "However, we came back home as we were all nervous and a bit superstitious watching him live in action."

It was a superstition that proved prophetically unnecessary. The 23-year-old left-arm spinner bowled India to their largest-ever Test victory — by an innings and 300 runs — finishing with match figures of seven wickets, including a devastating first-innings spell of 6 for 33 that reduced Afghanistan to 152. He was named Player of the Match in a game that ended inside three days.

## A Teacher's Son from the Border

Sri Ganganagar sits at Rajasthan's northwestern tip, irrigated by the Indira Gandhi Canal, closer to Lahore than to Jaipur. Cricket infrastructure there is sparse. Manav Suthar joined an academy at the age of 12 under two local coaches — Deepak Sir and Vinod Sir — and first made the Rajasthan Under-14 squad. That selection, his family says, was the moment they realised a career in cricket was possible.

What followed was a decade of patient accumulation. A breakthrough Ranji Trophy season in 2022-23 yielded 39 wickets in six matches for Rajasthan. An India A call-up against Australia A in 2025 produced a five-wicket haul in the first innings and three more in the second — the highest tally of the match. In the recently concluded Ranji season, a lethal 8 for 42 against Chhattisgarh cemented his credentials.

Rahul Dravid, one of India's finest batsmen and a meticulous judge of young talent, noticed early. But his advice was pointed: concentrate on bowling. Suthar was an all-rounder in the making, handy with the bat, but Dravid saw the spin as the sharper weapon. The advice stuck.

"It has been my dream from the very beginning to play for India and to play test cricket," Suthar told Reuters after the match. "So it was an incredible moment for me and honestly felt quite unreal."

## Stump to Stump, Over After Over

Captain Shubman Gill introduced Suthar shortly before tea on Day 2, after India had declared at a mammoth 564 for 8. On his fourth delivery in Test cricket, Suthar struck — Abdul Malik top-edged a sweep and was caught. It was the first time an Indian had taken a wicket in his very first over on Test debut in 25 years.

From there, the control was relentless. Suthar bowled stump to stump with sharp turn, mixing pace variations while maintaining an economy rate under 1.5 in his initial spell. Afghanistan's batters had no answers. Rahmanullah Gurbaz edged to slip. Afsar Zazai fell to the last ball of the day.

By the close of the second afternoon, Suthar had 3 for 21 from 15.5 overs. On Day 3, he added three more, completing a six-wicket haul. When Afghanistan followed on and crumbled again — this time for 112 — Suthar chipped in with another wicket.

"He bowled stump to stump and he was really disciplined in his bowling," said Afghanistan captain Hashmatullah Shahidi. "That's why we struggled against him. The pitch condition was changing and he was very disciplined."

## The Fifth Rajasthani to Wear the Test Cap

Suthar became only the fifth cricketer from Rajasthan to play Test cricket for India. His mother Sushila Devi was emotional when she spoke about the achievement: "He has reached this stage after 11 years of hard work. The entire family is overjoyed."

His sister Mansi, who first delivered the news of his India selection to the family, was equally overwhelmed. "This was his debut match and he performed exceptionally well. Across India, he is only the second player to take seven wickets on Test debut."

For the Indian diaspora, Suthar's story carries a familiar resonance. A father who is a schoolteacher. A family that left the stadium because watching was too nerve-wracking. A small town with no cricketing pedigree producing a match-winner at the highest level. These are the stories that cross borders.

## What Comes Next

Suthar plays for the Gujarat Titans in the IPL, where he debuted in 2024 but has been restricted to limited appearances — four matches in IPL 2026, yielding two wickets. The franchise format has yet to unlock his Test-match precision.

Reports suggest he is being considered for India's Test tour of Sri Lanka later this year, though he has not been included in the India A squad for the preceding warm-up matches. The next step, then, is uncertain — but his debut was as emphatic a statement of intent as any young spinner has made in recent memory.

"You have to keep bowling in the same area over and over again," Suthar reflected. "That's the most important thing in Test cricket. It's a format that demands a lot of patience."

At 23, patience is something Manav Suthar has in abundance. His family, watching from 1,500 kilometres away, would know that better than anyone.
